story.concept_sentence: A lighthouse keeper and her estranged brother must keep the lamp burning through one storm night while a ship runs blind towards the rocks.
story.logline: When the fuel barge fails to arrive, a stubborn lighthouse keeper must cross a flooding causeway with her estranged brother to keep the lamp lit before a stricken trawler hits the reef.
pitch: The Lighthouse Keeper is a contained survival drama set over one storm night on the Northumberland coast.
Mara has kept the light alone since their father drowned, and her brother Tom has come back only to sell it.
When the fuel fails and a trawler loses its instruments, the siblings must work together on the cliff and in the tower.
The film trades on elemental spectacle at a controlled budget, with two strong leads and a single location.
It sits alongside recent British survival dramas that travelled well with festival audiences and streamers.
synopsis: Mara prepares the lighthouse for a storm as her brother Tom arrives by boat, intent on selling the station.
The fuel barge fails to arrive and the radio picks up a trawler losing its instruments off the reef.
The siblings argue, reconcile and climb the cliff path to reach the old store, as the tide cuts them off.
In the climax they relight the lamp by hand and guide the trawler past the rocks; at dawn Tom chooses to stay.

creative.concept_and_premise: A clean, saleable survival premise with a clear ticking clock. The hook is elemental rather than high concept.
creative.story_and_structure: Tight three-act shape over one night. The midpoint reversal lands, but the second act repeats the climb beat.
creative.characters: Mara is a strong, active lead. Tom's turn is under-motivated until late. Elsie, the radio voice, is functional.
creative.dialogue: Economical and in character, with little exposition. Few memorable lines.
creative.themes_and_tone: Grief and duty, played straight. Tone is consistent and the genre promise is delivered.
creative.production_feasibility: Night exteriors, water work and a storm sequence drive cost; a single principal location contains it.

market.audience_profile: Upscale drama audience and festival goers.
market.release_pathway: Festival launch, then specialist theatrical in the UK and a streamer elsewhere.
market.sales_agent_tier: Mid-tier UK or European sales agent.
market.distributor_suitability: UK independent distributor; global streamer for rest of world.

comparables.title: Calm with Horses
comparables.relevance: Cast-led British drama on a contained budget.

comparables.title: Enys Men
comparables.relevance: Isolated coastal setting and festival route.

market.awards_festival_potential: BIFA and festival competition potential with the right director.
market.current_market_fit: Good fit for contained, cast-led British drama.
risks: Storm and water sequences may exceed a modest budget.
Value depends heavily on casting Mara.
Second-act repetition could slow the middle hour.

rewrite_priorities: Give Tom a concrete reason to stay by the midpoint.
Sharpen the trawler subplot so the stakes are felt earlier.
development_notes: Introduce the barge failure in scene one.
Give Elsie one decision that matters.
Land a final image that pays off the lamp.
develop.character_notes: Tom needs agency before the climax.
develop.dialogue_notes: Allow one argument to run long; the restraint elsewhere earns it.
develop.commercial_notes: Lean into the storm set piece in marketing.
develop.risk_if_budget_too_low: The storm reads as cheap and the film loses its spectacle.
develop.risk_if_budget_too_high: Recoupment needs a bigger cast than the material supports.
develop.to_justify_higher_budget: A star-level Mara and an extended rescue sequence.
cost_control_opportunities: Tank work rather than open sea.
Shoot the tower on a stage.

verdict.overall_assessment: A contained, castable survival drama that needs one more pass on the brother's arc.
verdict.commercial_potential: Moderate, rising sharply with a recognisable Mara.
verdict.reason_for_verdict: Strong engine and leads; the middle needs work before packaging.
verdict.best_next_step: Commission a focused rewrite on Tom and the second act, then approach casting.
